title: CASE -- A Traffic-Light / Sequencer State Machine
concept:
When a process moves through numbered steps (a sequencer, a batch phase, a
traffic light), CASE is cleaner than a stack of IF/ELSIF:

    CASE Seq_Step OF
        1: (* step 1 *)
        2: (* step 2 *)
        ELSE (* fallback *)
    END_CASE;

CASE tests an integer selector. Each numbered label runs its block, and you set
the selector to the NEXT step inside the block so the machine advances.

Real-world note: a production sequencer gates each transition on a condition --
usually a timer .DN bit (green for 30 s) or a sensor. Here we advance every scan
to focus on CASE structure; in the field you'd wrap each step with the timer
from Lesson 04.
ab_note:
Studio 5000 ST supports CASE ... OF ... END_CASE; with a DINT or INT selector.
This is the standard way to build a step-based sequencer in Logix ST instead of
a long ladder rung sequence.
siemens_note:
SCL uses the same CASE ... OF ... END_CASE; and also allows ranges (1..3) and
comma lists (1,3,5) as labels. Here we only need single integer labels.
task:
Build a 3-step traffic light with CASE on Seq_Step : INT. Outputs are
Green_Light, Yellow_Light, Red_Light (BOOL lamp outputs):

    Seq_Step = 1 : Green_Light  := TRUE; then advance to step 2
    Seq_Step = 2 : Yellow_Light := TRUE; then advance to step 3
    Seq_Step = 3 : Red_Light    := TRUE; then wrap back to step 1

Use CASE Seq_Step OF ... END_CASE;.
starter:
(* Lesson 05 -- CASE: a Traffic-Light / Sequencer State Machine *)

VAR
    Seq_Step     : INT := 1;  (* current state, 1..3 (starts at 1) *)
    Green_Light  : BOOL;      (* output *)
    Yellow_Light : BOOL;      (* output *)
    Red_Light    : BOOL;      (* output *)
END_VAR

Under  3:  add  Seq_Step := 1;  to loop the sequence.
